catalog.summary: Named, saved sets of filters for a list.

patternNote: No APG pattern covers a list of named views. The trigger opens a non-modal dialog (popover, aria-haspopup=dialog); each row's actions control is the Menu Button pattern, held by the menu family; everything inside the panel is native buttons, a form and a list in native tab order.
reference: Airtable views, Notion database views, Linear views (Revert), MUI X initialState/exportState, DevExtreme stateStoring
engine: @slotted/core/grid — SavedViewsState and its pure functions, serializeGridView, parseGridView, sameGridView

roles.trigger: button with aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded and aria-controls naming the panel
roles.panel: the popover's dialog, named by messages.label
roles.apply: button; aria-current=true on the view in use
roles.form: form, named by its field's label
roles.confirm: group, named by the question it asks

anatomy.root: a div: data-ui=saved-views, role=group, aria-label=messages.label, data-modified, data-open; the trigger and revert in one row
anatomy.trigger: a button naming the view in use — messages.builtIn when activeId is null — truncated with its whole name kept in the DOM, then modified, then a chevron; opens the layer
anatomy.modified: a span inside the trigger: a dot in the accent solid and the word messages.modified; present only with data-modified
anatomy.revert: a button beside the trigger that asks for the view in use again (action revert); present only with data-modified
anatomy.panel: a div inside the popover's content carrying data-ui=saved-views: the list, the save-as form and the footer, at --slotted-saved-views-panel-inline-size
anatomy.list: a ul, role=list: the built-in view first, then the saved views in the order the state holds them
anatomy.item: an li per view: data-current on the view in use, data-default on the default, data-built-in on the built-in view, data-editing while its form or confirmation replaces it
anatomy.apply: a button with the view's name that asks to apply it; aria-current=true and a check mark on the view in use
anatomy.default-mark: a span inside apply: the pin glyph and the visually hidden word messages.isDefault, so the name reads 'Late orders, default'
anatomy.actions: a button opening a menu for the row: Rename, Set as default, Delete; on the built-in view only Set as default
anatomy.form: a form holding a field — label messages.name, a text field, the error — and a submit and a cancel button: in the row for rename, above the footer for save-as
anatomy.footer: a div: Save (overwrites the view in use; disabled on the built-in view and while nothing is modified) and Save as new view…
anatomy.confirm: a div, role=group, in the row being deleted: the question messages.confirmDelete with the view's name, Delete in the danger tone and Cancel

attributes.data-modified: on the root while current differs from the active view
attributes.data-default: on the item of the view a visit opens on
attributes.data-built-in: on the item of the built-in view
attributes.data-editing: on the item whose rename form or delete confirmation is shown

onStateChange.payload: (state: SavedViewsState, request: { value, previous, reason, action, source, cancelled, cancel() })
onStateChange.from: apply, save, the form's submit (create, rename), the confirmation's Delete (remove), the menu's Set as default, the handle's apply (programmatic). Not emitted when the state would not change

onViewApply.payload: (view: GridView, request) — parseGridView(saved.view, columns), or builtIn for the built-in view
onViewApply.from: apply and revert, after the state request was not refused; the consumer writes the view into the grid

onOpenChange.from: the trigger, Escape, a press outside, apply and save (which close the layer), the handle

rules.modified: modified is !sameGridView(current, activeView, columns): the comparison of the two serialized lines of text, which already normalise an untouched order and width
rules.builtIn: the built-in view is first in the list, named messages.builtIn, applies builtIn, and its menu holds only Set as default; it is never renamed, overwritten or deleted
rules.save: Save overwrites the view in use with current; disabled on the built-in view and while the view is not modified
rules.saveAs: Save as new view… opens the form above the footer; its submit creates a view from current with a new id — crypto.randomUUID() when available, a counter otherwise — and makes it the view in use
rules.name: a name is trimmed; an empty name is refused with messages.empty and a name isViewNameTaken finds — or the built-in view's name — with messages.duplicate; the field is invalid and the error joins the input's description
rules.delete: Delete asks in the row, naming the view; confirming removes it with the reason remove. A deleted view that was in use or the default leaves the built-in view in its place; the grid keeps its arrangement, which then reads as modified
rules.focus: apply, save and revert close the layer and focus returns to the trigger; a submitted form focuses the row's apply; a cancelled form focuses the control that opened it; a confirmed delete focuses the previous row's apply
rules.announce: applied, saved (save and create), renamed, deleted and defaultChanged are announced politely through @slotted/core/live-announcer

keyboard.effect: on the trigger: opens the layer with focus on the view in use; on apply, revert, Save and the menu items: presses them
keyboard.focus: the apply of the view in use when opening

keyboard.effect: moves through the rows' apply and actions, then the footer, in native order
submits the name with the reason submit
with a form or a confirmation open: cancels the form and refuses the layer's close request; otherwise closes the layer
keyboard.focus: the control that opened the form, or the trigger

keyboard.key: ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Home / End / Escape in a row's menu
keyboard.focus: the menu's items, then the actions button

sharing.reason: who else sees a view is the application's permission model; the state is serializable and the consumer's store decides where it lives

reorder.reason: the list keeps the order views were created in; Airtable alone reorders views, and a dragged list of five names is not worth a drag session

search.reason: a reader keeps a handful of views; a search field above five rows is one more control than the list

gridState.reason: the family applies nothing to a grid; it emits the view and the consumer writes it, through persistedGridView or its own state

resolution: a word: the instance's messages, then the language in force, then English
